When the World Broke

There was a time before the fragments.

A time when reality existed as part of a vast, interconnected structure known as Adam Kadmon.

In that age, the systems that shaped the world—matter, imagination, knowledge, and life—were bound together within a single living architecture. Cities flourished. Knowledge flowed freely. The world was stable in ways that are now difficult to imagine.

Then something went wrong.

Something inside the structure failed.

And the world broke.

The Moment of Fracture

No one knows exactly how the Collapse began.

Some believe it was caused by a catastrophic mistake made by those who once understood the deeper systems of reality. Others believe the structure of Adam Kadmon simply could not endure the weight of the world it supported.

What is known is that when the Collapse occurred, it did not happen gradually.

Reality fractured.

Regions of the world separated from one another as the underlying structure holding them together shattered.

The once-connected landscape broke into isolated fragments — the hex-shaped territories that now define the world.

Entire regions vanished.
Others became unreachable.
Some were twisted by forces no one fully understands.

Civilizations fell almost overnight.

A World Left Behind

When the Collapse ended, the survivors found themselves living inside the fragments that remained.

The systems that once supported the world were damaged or incomplete. Infrastructure failed. Knowledge was lost. Strange phenomena began appearing in places where the structure of reality had torn.

But the world did not end.

Communities rebuilt what they could.
New societies emerged.
Explorers began mapping the fragments that remained.

Over time, people learned to live within the broken structure of the world.

But the scars of the Collapse are everywhere.

The Shattered Landscape

The hexes that make up the modern world are not random divisions of land.

They are fragments of a once-unified system.

Each hex represents a piece of the original structure of reality.

Some fragments remained stable after the Collapse.

Others became dangerous or corrupted.

Many contain remnants of the world that existed before — abandoned infrastructure, strange artifacts, and forgotten knowledge.

Exploring these fragments is one of the only ways to understand what was lost.

The Forces That Emerged

The Collapse did more than break geography.

It disrupted the deeper forces that once balanced the world.

In the absence of the original structure, new phenomena began appearing across the fragments:

• unstable magical currents
• corrupted landscapes
• creatures born from fractured reality
• strange echoes of the world that once existed

Some believe these forces are the natural result of a broken system.

Others believe something darker emerged during the Collapse.

Whatever the truth may be, the world has never fully recovered.

The Legacy of the Collapse

Even centuries later, the Collapse defines the shape of the world.

Every map reflects the fragments it left behind.

Every expedition uncovers traces of the world that existed before.

And every faction must decide how to live within the reality that remains.

Some factions seek to preserve what still survives.

Others attempt to exploit the instability of the fragments.

And a few believe that the broken structure of reality can still be repaired.

The Beginning of the Great Work

The Collapse created the problem that defines the age.

But it also created the possibility of something new.

If the fragments of reality can be stabilized…
If the connections between regions can be restored…
If the damaged systems of the world can be repaired…

Then the world might become whole again.

The effort to accomplish this impossible task is known as The Great Work.

And every faction working to rebuild the world now carries a small part of that responsibility.

In Simple Terms

The Collapse is the event that shattered reality into fragments.

The world did not end — but it was left incomplete.

Everything that happens in the campaign takes place within the broken structure the Collapse left behind.

And every action your faction takes helps determine whether the world will remain fractured… or slowly begin to heal.
